text:
A number of other mammal species, primarily rodents, have been observed. Based on trapping data, the deer mouse is the most common small mammal and is found in a wide range of habitat types. A small black tailed prairie dog colony numbering about 20 animals has been identified in the southeastern portion of Tract III. Muskrats are fairly common in stock watering ponds and along major streams. The desert cottontail rabbit is fairly common and generally is associated with creek bottom vegetation or other deciduous thickets.

Birds - Two hundred and thirty-six species of birds which have been observed or may occur in the project area are listed in (Appendix F). Information of food habits and habitats of family groups, sub-family
groups and individual species is also provided in Appendix F.
The sharp-tail grouse is common in the area and has been observed most often in grassland and silver sagebrush - grassland habitats. Five dancing grounds (leks) on Tract III and two on Tract II have been identified (Map II-4). In 1975, 47 dominant male sharp-tail grouse were observed displaying on dancing grounds on Tract III. Rippin and Boag (1974) stated that for each dominant male there is a subdominant male, and for each male there is a female; therefore the total spring population of sharp-tail grouse can be estimated by applying a factor of four to the number of dominant males observed. The estimated 1975 spring population on Tract III was 188, or about eight birds per square mile. Birds have been observed displaying irregularly at several other locations, but these probably were subdominant males prevented from displaying on established leks. Three additional leks have been observed one to two miles east of Tract III where a total of 44 dominant males were observed in 1975.
